title: Creating Turn Based Combat (Single Character) with Claude Code
author: bahamutech
selftext:
(Note: Sorry last post video quality kinda sucked)  
  
Playable Campaign (vertical slice): Fox Samurai 21 battle (has an ending)  
[https://bahamutech.itch.io/actrinity](https://bahamutech.itch.io/actrinity)

Developed with Claude Code for almost all code.

**Stack:**  
Framework - React  
Art - [retrodiffusion.ai](http://retrodiffusion.ai)  
Music - Suno

**The Game:**  
You control a single character  
You queue 3 actions per round. Enemies queue 1-2 (bosses get 3).  
All actions resolve sequentially based on speed. Each action slot applies a flat speed penalty:

* Slot 1: no penalty
* Slot 2: -20 speed
* Slot 3: -40 speed

So a character with 100 base speed would act at 100, 80, and 60.  
Actions can also influence the speed, power, or effect of later actions in the queue.

**System:**  
Actions run through a fixed pipeline of phases:

PRE\_ACTION → Resource Deduct → Retarget → ON\_INCOMING → Tag Interaction → IMBUE → DELIVERY → INJECT\_MULT → INJECT\_FLAT → DAMAGE\_REDUCE → ON\_RECEIVE → SELF TAGS → POST\_ATTACK

Turn boundaries also run: ON\_TURN\_START → END\_OF\_TURN

Buffs and debuffs are Tags. A Tag just declares which phases it cares about and what it does when those phases run. To add a new mechanic, write a handler file, register the tag, and that's it, nothing else in the engine changes.

Actions are pure data. They declare what tags to apply and to who. The tag handlers do the actual work.

Right now map, battle scenario, attacks, and new enemies can be set up entirely through JSON. I design them and AI easily implements them.

Originally attacks were just CSS animations. I recently integrated PIXI.js and built a separate tool for making animations. You write an attack as a JSON file that the game itself reads and applies. I was able to easily make slash animations by prompting AI to write the JSON.

**My Goal:**

* I want to see how far this combat system can go.
* To understand the foundation, to be able to create a full fledged RPG in the future, Actrinity 2.
* (plan to use AI to re-translate the combat\_engine to another framework)

**Current Plans:**

* See if it's possible to make CSS behave the same way I did for the PIXI interpreter.
* Each campaign is a way to test and push new mechanics into the combat engine.
* Make Monk Campaign (state-based influenced actions). Map Rework (more thematic?).
* Rework on Samurai Campaign v2 (rework the mechanics of Samurai, clash logic new dodge).

comments.author: Redditry199
comments.body:
Honestly?  
The UI is clean, the sound is cute, the music is cool, the art is simple and pretty.

Combat is a bit brain dead and boring, I think the way cards are picked and played is not very engaging, card game have draws and piles and mechanics to keep you engaged but spending all the first level just selecting 3 attacks is not the most engaging gameplay.

Nonetheless great work.

replies.author: bahamutech
replies.body:
Appreciate the kind words, and fair criticism.

I get what you mean. I'm not aiming for a traditional deckbuilder. My game is actually more in line with classic Dragon Quest combat. What I'm trying to find is the depth of having a single character that can compare to a full party-based game.

The core gameplay is based around speed and queuing actions. The player has 3 actions and enemies have 1-2 (Bosses 3). All actions resolve sequentially based on speed, and each slot applies a flat speed penalty. One of the main strategies comes from manipulating that order. For example Storm Strike reduces the targets' speed by -20, and Shinsoku ignores the speed penalty and boosts your next action speed by 20.

Feel free to give it a play to see it in action. The speed abilities unlock a bit later in the campaign.

replies.author: ikatakko
replies.body:
i love classic dragon quest so this should appeal to me but it doesnt it just seems like a generic card battler made with AI 

i'd suggest revamping the UI to resemble an actual classic rpg with menu based selections and first person attack animations if dq is truly the inspiration otherwise it looks okay albeit a bit generic but i certainly wouldn't be able to tell it was inspired by dragon quest if that was the goal

replies.author: bahamutech
replies.body:
Dragon Quest combat was probably the wrong term to use in this case.   
  
It's more branching off from traditional turn-based combat.   
I replaced standard attacks/spells with a card UI because I felt that cards were better for visualizing the actions. It's more similar to hotbars in mmorpg, except card shape.
